question: Find the simple interest (in ₹) on ₹2000 at 6.75% per annum rate of interest for the period from 3 February 2023 to 17 April 2023.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total time from 3 Feb to 17 Apr = 25 days (Feb) + 31 days (Mar) + 17 days (Apr) = 73 days.

Time (T) in years = 73 ÷ 365 = 1/5 years.

Using the Direct Simple Interest formula: SI = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

⇒ SI = (2000 × 6.75 × 1/5) ÷ 100 = 20 × 1.35 = 27

**∴ The correct answer is ₹27.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Principal (P) = ₹2000

Rate of Interest (R) = 6.75% per annum

Time Period = 3 February 2023 to 17 April 2023

 
• 
 

 
 
 
 
 
 3 Feb
 (25 days)

 (31 days)

 17 Apr

 Total = 73 days
 
 
 P = ₹2000 | R = 6.75% | T = 73/365 y

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

**Calculations:**

⇒ Number of days in February 2023 (a non-leap year) = 28

⇒ Remaining days in February = 28 − 3 = 25 days

⇒ Days in March = 31 days

⇒ Days in April = 17 days

⇒ Total Time (T) in days = 25 + 31 + 17 = 73 days

⇒ Time (T) in years = 73 ÷ 365 = 1/5 years

⇒ SI = [2000 × 6.75 × (1/5)] ÷ 100

⇒ SI = 20 × 6.75 × (1/5)

⇒ SI = 4 × 6.75

⇒ SI = 27

**∴ The correct answer is ₹27.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Rule for Counting Days in SI

When calculating simple interest between two exact dates, either the starting day or the ending day is included, but never both. Most commonly, the starting date is excluded and the end date is included.

Leap Year Identification

A year is a leap year if it is perfectly divisible by 4. However, century years must be divisible by 400. In non-leap years (like 2023), February has exactly 28 days.

Common Days to Years Conversions

Standard fractional year conversions used frequently in exams: 73 days = 1/5 year, 146 days = 2/5 year, 219 days = 3/5 year, and 292 days = 4/5 year.
